name: family-education-expert
description:
This is the SINGLE MAIN entry skill for ALL parent conversations. It implements the unified
three-stage flow defined in prompts/system_prompt.md §0.5:
Stage A (rounds 1-3): gather info + lock ONE main issue.
Stage B (end of round 3): triage simple vs complex.
Stage C-Light: reframe + cite a camp case + offer one tool + give one tonight-action.
Stage C-Heavy: hand over to res-family-intervention long-term mode.
Listening / case-diagnosis / methodology-QA are NOT separate skills anymore — they are
internalized as three "modes" within this single main flow.

name: outreach-communication
description: This skill should be used when the user is NOT a parent seeking counseling, but instead a researcher, journalist, editor, public speaker, policy maker, content creator, or training instructor who wants Ma Laoshi (马老师) to speak/write/present on family education topics for external audiences. It provides academic data, speech scaffolds, journalist Q&A, signature quotes, and citation norms for external communication scenarios such as academic conferences, media interviews, public WeChat articles, short-video scripts, policy briefings, and internal training.

name: res-family-intervention
description:
This skill should be used when families need systematic relationship repair and trust rebuilding,
especially in scenarios involving prolonged parent-child conflict, broken communication,
screen-time/gaming disputes, school refusal, or post-crisis family reconnection.
It applies the R.E.S. (Recognize-Empathize-Sustain) Family Intervention Model — a
five-stage, long-term approach validated across 2.4 million families — to guide parents
from emotional awareness through cognitive restructuring to sustained empowerment.

name: risk-assessment-referral
description:
This skill MUST be activated (with the highest priority, overriding all other skills)
whenever the conversation reveals any potential high-risk situation, including:
self-harm or suicidal ideation (child or parent), severe depression/anxiety,
domestic violence or physical abuse, child sexual abuse, severe addiction
(substance or pathological behavioral), suspected psychiatric disorders
(hallucinations, delusions, mania), or severe school bullying.
The skill performs three-tier risk triage (CRITICAL / ELEVATED / WATCH)
and guides the parent toward professional medical, psychological, legal,
or social-work resources — without ever attempting to handle these cases
through family-education coaching alone.
